name: query_metrics
description:
Query an instant vector at the investigation end time.

        Use when sample values are needed to check a hypothesis. Reuse known
        names and labels; discover_metrics is optional if they are confirmed.
        Skip this tool when existing evidence already answers the question.
        Returns normalized observations with evidence IDs, or empty-query
        guidance without evidence IDs. An empty result does not establish
        health: check names, labels and sample availability before retrying.

        Conditional example: ONLY if discovery returned request_count_total
        and the label job="orders", query_metrics with expression
        'request_count_total{job="orders"}' can inspect those samples.
        If names or labels are unknown, discover them instead of guessing.

inputSchema.description: Query an instant vector at the application-selected end time.

expression.title: Expression
expression.description: PromQL expression returning an instant vector, using confirmed metric names and label values. Not a bare range vector or scalar. Query time is fixed to the investigation end by the application.

inputSchema.title: MetricQuery

name: discover_metrics
description:
Discover metric names and label examples before writing PromQL.

        Use when relevant names or labels are unknown, including after an
        empty query with suspected mismatched names/labels. Reuse previously
        discovered metadata instead of rediscovering it for every query.
        Skip discovery when names/labels are known or evidence is sufficient.
        The application fixes the investigation window; do not supply dates.

        Returns metrics containing metric, label_keys and example_labels.
        Empty example_labels means no examples were included, not that the
        metric has no labels; pass its exact returned name as metric to inspect
        it. possibly_truncated, omitted_metrics and labels_truncated mark
        incomplete coverage. Empty discovery may mean service labels differ;
        bounded global discovery can reveal them. Absence never proves health.
        Metadata has no evidence IDs or sample values and cannot be cited.

        Examples: If the incident names orders and metric names are unknown,
        discover_metrics(service="orders") finds candidates to query.
        If retained evidence already supports a user's explanation request,
        answer directly without discovery or another metric query.

inputSchema.description: Select a bounded metric-name or label catalogue.

service.title: Service
service.description: Exact service value matched against service_name, service or job labels, not a substring or regex. Omit or use null for a bounded global catalogue when these labels are unknown.

metric.title: Metric
metric.description: One exact metric name returned by discovery, not PromQL or a regex. Set it to inspect that metric's label examples; omit or use null to discover distinct metric names first.

limit.title: Limit
limit.description: Maximum distinct names and maximum series inspected per metadata request (1-50, default 20), not an evidence count or time range. Results may be incomplete even at this limit.

inputSchema.title: MetricDiscovery

name: search_traces
description: Find recent Jaeger traces for one service in the incident window.

name: get_trace_detail
description:
Inspect a known trace: return error spans plus up to 20 longest successful spans, including service, operation, duration_ms, is_error and parent_span_id when available. Use successful spans to investigate latency even when there are no errors. Parent and child durations overlap; do not sum them. Results are bounded, not a complete span tree. TraceMind filters observations to its investigation window. 

        Use its returned attributes.trace_id, not the evidence's id. If no
        trace ID is available, search_traces or search_logs first. Do not
        reconstruct a trace ID from an abbreviated value.

inputSchema.description: Require an actual Jaeger trace ID rather than an evidence UUID.

trace_id.title: Trace Id
trace_id.description: Copy the exact attributes.trace_id from returned trace or log evidence: a 16 or 32 character hexadecimal Jaeger ID. Not an evidence UUID or span_id. Never invent or pad an ID.

inputSchema.title: TraceDetail

name: search_logs
description: Find OpenSearch logs for one service, optionally matching text. Results are a bounded sample; absence of a message does not prove absence of a fault. Event time is preferred; when it is absent or zero, use observation time, marked by timestamp_source=observedTimestamp in evidence. Observation time is not proof of the exact event occurrence time.

inputSchema.description: Select service logs with an optional body-text filter.

service.title: Service
service.description: Exact telemetry service name. Not an operation name or a list of services.

text.title: Text
text.description: Optional log-body search terms. Omit or use null to apply no body-text filter. Not a trace ID filter or a regex.

inputSchema.title: LogSearch
